text: A recall lets voters remove an elected official
before the term ends.
Proposition five changes what happens next.
It does not eliminate the power to recall
state officials.
Proposition five removes the replacement question.
The office would be filled through succession, appointment,
or a separate election, depending on the office
and when the recall happens.
If a legislator is recalled, a special election
would generally fill the seat.
Vacancies in most other state offices would be
filled by gubernatorial appointment.
A voter might want removal considered on its
own, rather than as a shortcut for a
candidate with limited support.
Another voter could object to giving appointments or
automatic succession a larger role.
Yes changes the replacement process;
no keeps the replacement question on recall ballots.
